newsitem.title: USA: U.S. officials seek Mexican in deaf mute scandal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. officials seek Mexican in deaf mute scandal.

text.p: Police were searching on Monday for the leader of a smuggling ring that forced dozens of deaf mute Mexicans into servitude selling trinkets on the streets of New York.
Seven people have been arrested on charges of forcing the deaf mute Mexicans to work for them.

Officials who rescued 57 people from two cramped apartments in the New York City borough of Queens over the weekend said there were indications that they were kidnapped and smuggled into the United States from Mexico through California and Texas.

Police in the United States and Mexico were searching for a Mexican man believed to be the leader of the operation. He was identified by police as Reinaldo Paoletti. Four of those arrested were also members of the Paoletti family.
Authorities believe they recruited their victims from homes and schools for the deaf and mute in Mexico, promising them a better life in the United States.

Instead they were forced under threat of beatings to work as vendors of trinkets like key chains, baseballs, pens and toys on the streets and subways. They were allowed to keep only 20 percent of the takings, 80 percent going to those who accused of running the operation.
Of the 57 rescued, there were 27 men, 18 women, including three who were pregnant, and 12 children ranging in age from six months to 16 years, officials said.
They said the Mexicans were in the custody of New York City authorities and the American Red Cross was providing them with housing and food until their immigration status was determined.
